name: Introduction and overview — County-class Destroyer — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — County-class Destroyer
description: Introduction and overview of the County-class Destroyer: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Royal Navy's County class — eight ships built in the 1960s — were large guided-missile destroyers built around the Seaslug surface-to-air missile. They were the last Royal Navy ships with significant gun armament (twin 4.5-inch). Counties served in the Falklands War; two were sold to Chile and Pakistan. Baseline facts: Royal Navy missile destroyer; 8 built; Seaslug SAM; Falklands service..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
